card.title: Mark a version with a tag
card.blurb: Pin a name to one commit so you can find that exact version again. Add one tag at `HEAD`, then one tag on an older commit.
hero.title: Mark a version with a tag
intro.0: A branch moves as work continues. Sometimes you need a name that stays fixed, like a release marker. That is what a tag is: a label pinned to one commit. Here you mark the commit you are on, then mark an earlier one, without moving `HEAD` or changing any branch.
task.1.title: Name the version you are standing on
task.1.context:
A tag is a name pinned to one commit, and it does not move when new commits appear.

This project has shipped before, so some version names are already taken. `git tag` on its own lists them. Find out which numbers are gone, then put the next one on the commit you are on.
task.1.goal.0: Run `git tag` to see which version names already exist.
task.1.goal.1: Run `git log --oneline` to see where the last one was pinned.
task.1.goal.2: Pin the next version number to the commit you are standing on.
task.1.goal.3: Move nothing else - stay on the same branch and commit.
task.2.title: Name a commit you are not standing on
task.2.context:
`HEAD~1` means one commit before where you stand, `HEAD~2` two before, and so on. That is how you name a commit without moving to it.

Four commits sit on `main` and none of them is tagged. One of them is the release - its message says so. The log is the only thing here that tells you which.
task.2.goal.0: Run `git log --oneline` and read the four messages.
task.2.goal.1: Pin `v1` to the commit whose message calls it a release.
task.2.goal.2: Pin `v0` to the very first commit, at the bottom of the log.
task.2.goal.3: Do not move `HEAD` and do not move any branch.
task.3.title: Mark a version with a tag - recap
task.3.context: A tag is fixed; a branch keeps moving.
task.3.summaryIntro: A tag is a stable label on one commit. It helps you return to that exact point later, even after many new commits. The log is where you work out which commit deserves the label.
task.3.summaryItems.0.title: Tag -
task.3.summaryItems.0.text: a name pinned to one commit that does not move with later work.
task.3.summaryItems.1.title: `git tag` -
task.3.summaryItems.1.text: with nothing after it, lists the names already taken, so you know which one is free.
task.3.summaryItems.2.title: `git tag v2` -
task.3.summaryItems.2.text: marks the commit you are on now, with no checkout and no branch movement.
task.3.summaryItems.3.title: `git tag v1 HEAD~1` -
task.3.summaryItems.3.text: marks an older commit by revision, while you stay where you are.
task.3.summaryItems.4.title: Branch vs tag -
task.3.summaryItems.4.text: branches move as you commit; tags stay pinned at one version.
task.3.summaryClose: Next: merge a branch back into `main` and read what kind of merge happened.
concept.gt-tag.def: A name pinned to one commit that never moves, for marking a version worth finding again.
